channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Khartoum drone strike kills five Sudan NGO reports
item.description: Israeli forces expanded the "orange line" in Gaza, tightening movement restrictions and raising deadly risks for civilians. The expanded zone now covers more areas, further isolating the Palestinian territory. The attack, the second in a week, follows months of relative calm in the city after government forces regained control.

item.title: Taiwan leader makes delayed visit to Eswatini after China objections
item.description: Taiwan's leader visited Eswatini, a move delayed due to Chinese objections. The visit comes after months of diplomatic efforts to strengthen ties between the two nations. Taiwan leader makes delayed visit to Eswatini after China objections.

item.title: Hobbesian Enmity and Resource Wars in Apocalyptic Popular Culture - E-International Relations
item.description: This article discusses the theme of Hobbesian enmity and resource wars in apocalyptic popular culture. It explores how these themes are represented in various forms of media, including films and literature.

item.title: Israel’s expanding ‘orange line’ tightens deadly no-go zones in Gaza
item.description: Israel's military expanded the "orange line" in Gaza, deepening movement restrictions and increasing risks for civilians. The expanded zone now covers more areas, further isolating the Palestinian territory. Israel’s expanding “orange line” is deepening movement restrictions across Gaza, raising deadly risks for civilians.

item.title: Leclerc rows back from 'harsh' criticism of Antonelli's driving
item.description: Charles Leclerc softened his criticism of Antonio Antonelli's driving after initially calling it harsh. Leclerc's comments followed a collision between the two drivers in a recent racing event. Leclerc rows back from 'harsh' criticism of Antonelli's driving.

item.title: Oil tanker hijacked off coast of Yemen and taken towards Somalia
item.description: An oil tanker was hijacked off the coast of Yemen and taken towards Somalia, the second such incident in the area in 10 days. The hijacking raised concerns about maritime security in the region.

item.title: May 4, 2026 | "How Hezbollah Makes Peace between Lebanon and Israel Impossible" with Dr. Ibtissam
item.description: Dr. Ibtissam Klait spoke about Hezbollah's role in preventing peace between Lebanon and Israel. The discussion highlighted the group's influence on regional politics and its impact on the Middle East peace process.

item.title: Iran military official says renewed war with U.S. 'likely'
item.description: Iran says war with the US is likely after the US warned shipping companies about sanctions for paying Iran to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: NATO is trying to "understand the details" of the US decision to withdraw troops from Germany
item.description: NATO is reviewing the US decision to withdraw troops from Germany. Details are being assessed. NATO is trying to "understand the details" of the US decision to withdraw troops from Germany Українські Національні Новини (УНН).

item.title: Nobel laureate Mohammadi's life in Iran's hands, Nobel committee chief says
item.description: The Nobel committee chief said Iran controls Nobel laureate Mohammadi's life. His situation is uncertain. Nobel laureate Mohammadi's life in Iran's hands, Nobel committee chief says.

item.title: Yemen reports hijacked oil tanker headed for Somalia
item.description: Yemen reported a hijacked oil tanker heading for Somalia, the fourth vessel hijacking near Somalia in recent weeks. The incident marks at least the fourth vessel hijacking near Somalia in recent weeks.

item.title: Spain’s Sanchez demands Netanyahu free Spaniard seized on aid flotilla
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez demanded Israel release a Spaniard seized on an aid flotilla. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is demanding Israel to release the 'abducted' Spaniard taken from the flotilla.

item.title: Thirteen killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, health ministry says
item.description: Thirteen people were killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon. Four women and a child were among the dead. Four women and a child are among the dead, as fighting between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah continues despite a ceasefire.

item.title: Mexican governor indicted by US steps down
item.description: Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha Moya stepped down after being indicted by the US. He was accused of protecting the Sinaloa cartel and taking millions in bribes. Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha Moya has been accused of protecting the powerful Sinaloa cartel and helping it smuggle drugs into the US, allegedly taking in millions of dollars in bribes.

item.title: Germany says US troop withdrawal 'foreseeable' as Nato seeks clarification
item.description: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius expects the US to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said the US decision to withdraw 5,000 troops was to be expected.

item.title: Trump tells Congress ceasefire means he does not need their approval for Iran war
item.description: US President Trump claims the Iran ceasefire terminates hostilities, arguing he no longer needs congressional approval for war. This assertion contradicts existing law requiring congressional authorisation for military action. The president writes that hostilities "have terminated" because of the ceasefire, arguing he does not need congressional authorisation.

item.title: U.S. Fast-Tracks Arms Deals Valued at $8.6 Billion to Mideast Partners
item.description: The US fast-tracked $8.6 billion in arms deals to Mideast partners, bypassing congressional review, amid repeated Iranian attacks. The Persian Gulf countries and Israel have faced repeated Iranian attacks during the U. S.-Israeli war with Iran.

item.title: US warns shipping firms over Iran ‘toll’ payments; Gulf bases ‘heavily damaged’: 10 developments
item.description: The US warned shipping firms over Iran toll payments and reported Gulf bases were heavily damaged. US warns shipping firms over Iran ‘toll’ payments; Gulf bases ‘heavily damaged’: 10 developments.

item.title: U.S. to Withdraw 5,000 Troops From Germany. But Thousands Will Remain.
item.description: The US will withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany, but thousands will remain, with tens of thousands of personnel still stationed there. The U. S. military has tens of thousands of personnel in Germany, more than in any other foreign country but Japan.

item.title: Fighting reaches outskirts of Ukraine's stronghold Kostiantynivka
item.description: Fighting reached the outskirts of Kostiantynivka, a Ukrainian stronghold in the east, which is part of a fortified belt. Kostiantynivka, ​along with other cities, forms a so-called fortress ⁠belt in the country’s east - an area well fortified by the Ukrainian military.
